Class MapLineItem

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.item.AItem
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.item.AMapItem
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.item.MapLineItem
All Implemented Interfaces:
IFeedbackProvider, IDrawable, EventListener
public class MapLineItem extends AMapItem
A map-native line item defined by two geographic endpoints and rendered as a seam-aware great-circle route.

Conceptual model

Unlike edu.cnu.mdi.item.LineItem, which stores a straight segment in ordinary world (projection-space) coordinates, MapLineItem stores its geometry in geographic coordinates:

  • _startLatLon — geographic start point in radians (x = longitude, y = latitude)
  • _endLatLon — geographic end point in radians (x = longitude, y = latitude)

When drawn, the item is projected and sampled as a great-circle route through MapGraphics, giving the familiar "airline route" appearance on a map.

Interaction model

  • Creation — use the ordinary straight-line rubberband. The tool converts its two screen endpoints to geographic coordinates via MapContainer.localToLatLon(Point, Point2D.Double) and constructs a MapLineItem.
  • Drag — moves both geographic endpoints by the great-circle displacement implied by the mouse movement, preserving great-circle length and initial bearing exactly.
  • Resize — replaces the selected endpoint with the current geographic cursor location.
  • Rotate — rotates both endpoints around the geodesic midpoint by the screen-space angle dragged, preserving great-circle length from the midpoint to each endpoint. See Rotation semantics below.

Focus and selection handles

The item focus is the exact geodesic midpoint of the arc (computed via MapGraphics.greatCircleEndPoint(Point2D.Double, double, double) at half the arc length). The two selection handles are the projected screen positions of the geographic endpoints.

Rotation semantics

Rotation is well-defined and physically meaningful for a great-circle line. The pivot is the geodesic midpoint (the item focus). The angular delta is the screen-space three-point angle dragged by the user (identical to how the base PathBasedItem handles rotation). The two half-lengths from the midpoint to each endpoint are preserved; only the bearings change.

Because a great-circle has two distinct initial bearings (from start→midpoint and from end→midpoint), both must be rotated independently using MapGraphics.greatCircleAzimuth(Point2D.Double, Point2D.Double) and MapGraphics.greatCircleEndPoint(Point2D.Double, double, double). This keeps the arc symmetric around its pivot for any rotation angle.

The AItem._azimuth field inherited from AItem is used as the cumulative screen-space rotation angle (in degrees) for display purposes (e.g. the rotation handle position). The geographic geometry is the authoritative state; _azimuth is purely a display aid that accumulates across multiple rotate gestures.

Geometry and caching

The projected route is cached as a MapGraphics.ProjectedMapShape after drawing. That cached shape is used for hit testing and bounds. The cache is cleared whenever the item is marked dirty.

Note on getWorldBounds()

The inherited AItem.getWorldBounds() contract requires a projection-space bounding rectangle. For a great-circle arc this rectangle is not computable without a projection reference, so this method returns a simple longitude/latitude bounding box of the two endpoints. This is conservative: it may miss the arc's apex if the arc bulges significantly above or below the chord (e.g. a trans-polar route). All visibility and hit-testing that matters uses the screen-space getBounds(IContainer) path through the cached projected shape, which is exact.

    • modify

      public void modify()
      Continues an interactive modification.

      Drag

      Moves the start endpoint by the great-circle displacement between the drag start and current mouse positions (converted to geographic coordinates). The end endpoint is then recomputed from the new start using the preserved great-circle azimuth and length, keeping the arc's shape invariant across latitudes.

      Resize

      Replaces the selected endpoint (index 0 = start, 1 = end) with the current geographic cursor location. The opposite endpoint is unchanged.

      Rotate

      Rotates both endpoints around the geodesic midpoint (the item focus) by the screen-space three-point angle dragged by the user. Both half-arc lengths (midpoint→start and midpoint→end) are preserved; only the bearings change. The AItem._azimuth field accumulates the total screen-space rotation for display purposes.

      Specified by:
      modify in class AItem

    • getWorldBounds

      public Rectangle2D.Double getWorldBounds()
      Returns an approximate world-space bounding rectangle.

      This returns a simple longitude/latitude bounding box of the two endpoints. It is provided only to satisfy the AItem contract. It may under-estimate the true extent of high-latitude arcs that bulge significantly above or below the chord between the endpoints. All visibility and hit-testing that matters uses the exact screen-space bounds available through getBounds(IContainer).

      Specified by:
      getWorldBounds in class AItem
      Returns:
      a lon/lat bounding rectangle in radians, or null if either endpoint is absent

    • translateWorld

      public void translateWorld(double dx, double dy)
      Translates the item by raw longitude and latitude offsets in radians.

      This is a pragmatic translation: for small distances and mid-latitude items it works well. At high latitudes the longitudinal scale diverges from the latitudinal scale, so a northward mouse drag may introduce a small longitudinal error. A future implementation could convert the pixel delta to a geodesic bearing and length, then call MapGraphics.greatCircleEndPoint(Point2D.Double, double, double), but that requires a MapContainer reference not available here.

      Specified by:
      translateWorld in class AItem
      Parameters:
      dx - longitude offset in radians
      dy - latitude offset in radians

    • startModification

      public void startModification()
      Classify and begin a drag, resize, or rotate modification.

      Priority: rotate (if start point is in rotation handle) → resize (if start point is in a selection handle) → drag (otherwise).

      This method is a no-op if AItem._modification is null.

      Overridden to attach the MapLineItem.MapLineStartState snapshot with the current screen-space azimuth baked in, so that sequential rotate gestures accumulate correctly.
